# Genius Group Launches GENIUSpark to Build and Operate Community-First AI Data Centers, Targeting an Initial 100 MW of AI Compute


October 26, 2026 8:00am EDT[Download as PDF](https://d1io3yog0oux5.cloudfront.net/_2ff5d3ddef955ee13ff0305ef93edd40/geniusgroup/news/2026-10-26_Genius_Group_Launches_GENIUSpark_to_Build_and_266.pdf)


***Genius Group Board approves the incorporation of GENIUSpark to build, own and operate community-first AI data centers through joint ventures with AI companies, data center operators and power partners worldwide.***


***GENIUSpark intends to deliver fully integrated AI data center locations including powered land, colocation, AI compute, community reskilling and a local AI treasury, with an initial target of 100 MW and a long-term goal of 1 GW.***


***Each 9.9 MW GENIUSpark site is designed with the goal to generate more than $100 million in annual revenue at a 35% net profit margin, with 10% of net profit returned to its host community through Genius Group’s Genius City model.***


***The first GENIUSpark joint ventures are in advanced discussions, with binding agreements expected to be announced in the coming weeks.***


***Launch comes as AI demand for power outruns grid supply and the neocloud market is forecast to grow from $25 billion in 2025 to nearly $400 billion by 2031*** *\[1\]* *.*


**SINGAPORE, Oct. 26, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) --** Genius Group Limited (NYSE American: GNS) ( **"Genius Group"** , **"GNS"** or the **"Company"** ), a leading AI-powered education group, today announced the launch of GENIUSpark, its community-first AI power company. Following approval by its Board of Directors, the Company is incorporating GENIUSpark as a wholly owned subsidiary to build, own and operate AI data centers together with the communities that host them, through joint ventures with AI companies, data center operators and power partners worldwide.


**GENIUSpark: The Community Solution to the AI Revolution**


GENIUSpark evolves Genius Group’s Genius City model into AI infrastructure. Each GENIUSpark site combines five layers in one project: low-cost power, powered land and colocation, high-performance AI compute sold as compute and inference capacity to enterprise, platform and education customers, community reskilling, and a local AI treasury. Sites are sized at up to 9.9 MW: small enough to be approved and powered in months rather than years, and large enough to potentially generate more than $100 million in annual revenue.


Every GENIUSpark site is designed around its host community. Genius Group will deliver local schooling, AI and entrepreneurship programs and reskilling into the jobs each site creates, based on its Genius City model, and 10% of each site’s net profit will be paid into a locally governed Community Fund. Over time, each fund is designed to build its own local AI treasury, making residents stakeholders in the AI infrastructure they host.


GENIUSpark targets an initial 100 MW of AI compute, representing a target of $1 billion of annual revenue under its intended model, and a long-term goal of 1 GW.


The Company is currently focused on launching GENIUSpark in countries that have low cost, accessible power together with high market demand and government support, commencing with Canada, Australia and Indonesia. In each region, GENIUSpark plans to partner with power producers, data center developers and AI companies, with each site held and funded in its own local project company.


The Company is in advanced discussions on the first GENIUSpark locations, and anticipates the first binding agreements to be announced in the coming weeks.


**Solving the Two Challenges of the AI Build-Out: AI Power and Community Empowerment**


TrendForce forecasts global data center power demand to rise 31% this year to 161 GW, and to reach 490.7 GW by 2030, leaving a projected 268 GW gap against available grid capacity\[2\]. In Alberta, large-load connection requests climbed above 16 GW, against an interim limit of 1,200 MW for new loads of 75 MW or more through 2027 and 2028\[3\]. GENIUSpark sites are sized below 10 MW and can bring their own behind-the-meter power, allowing them to move in months rather than waiting years in the grid queue.


The second challenge is community support and benefits. Nearly $200 billion of U.S. data center projects, across about 120 projects, were blocked or delayed in the first half of 2026, and a Gallup survey found that seven in ten Americans oppose an AI data center in their local area\[4\]. Communities are asking who pays for the power, how much water is used, and whether local people will share in the benefits.


Roger James Hamilton, Founder and CEO of Genius Group, said *"Every AI data center needs two things: AI power and community empowerment. Power can be solved with access and capital. We believe community empowerment is solved with our GENIUSpark model of local reskilling, education and a local AI treasury that makes every community member a stakeholder. GENIUSpark is the community solution for the AI revolution: every site we build trains local students and workers for the jobs AI creates, and returns 10% of its profits to the town that hosts it."*


*"Our first milestone is 100 MW, starting with our pilot in the coming months, and our long-term target is a gigawatt of community-first AI within the next decade. We are building GENIUSpark to be the partner of choice for AI companies and data center operators that want to grow with the support of the communities they serve."*


Suraj Naik, Head of AI at Genius Group, said *"AI is moving from training to inference, and inference needs to run close to the people and businesses that use it. Data residency rules and the need for low latency are pushing compute out of a handful of mega campuses and into local sites. That is where GENIUSpark is built: smaller, faster to power, closer to users, and run with the communities around them. Our own Genius OS platform will be one of the first customers on GENIUSpark compute."*


**Unit Economics of the GENIUSpark Model**


Under the GENIUSpark model, each full 9.9 MW site is targeted to generate more than $100 million in annual revenue and approximately $35 million in annual net profit, a 35% net profit margin, with a target of $3.5 million a year paid to the local Community Fund and more than 1,000 students, entrepreneurs and skilled workers trained each year.


GENIUSpark targets a build cost of under $10 million per MW of compute, using refurbished accelerators bought in bulk, modular halls and on-site power.


Gaurav Dama, Chief Financial Officer of Genius Group, said *"GENIUSpark is designed to fund its own growth. Our intention is for each site to be financed at the project level, with a combination of debt and equity financing shared with our joint venture partners, so we can scale without straining our balance sheet. While final pro forma financials will be on a site-by-site basis, our model targets a 35% net margin with 10% of net profit returned to the local community. This gives a benefit to each community and to our Genius Group investors. Our plan is for GENIUSpark to add a significant cash-generating AI infrastructure business to our education operations and our Bitcoin and AI treasury."*

**About Genius Group**


Genius Group (NYSE: GNS) is a global education group delivering AI powered, education and acceleration solutions for the future of work. Genius Group serves 6 million users in over 100 countries through its Genius City model and online digital marketplace of AI training, AI tools and AI talent. It provides personalized, entrepreneurial AI pathways combining human talent with AI skills and AI solutions at the individual, enterprise and government level. To learn more, please visit geniusgroup.ai
